decisions.statement: A subject is named by the slug a deploy would be handed.
The workstation kind is one subject, since the kind is put up whole.
That one subject is the page type's own page rather than any service's page.
The ios apps are read from their own reader rather than from the page index.
An ios app's cooldown is read off its page, as every other subject's is.
Every other kind is every page of that kind a deploy reads as that kind.
A page whose slug a deploy reads as another kind is no subject of the kind it is filed under.
A deploy of a web app's slug puts up the cluster service beside that web app.
A page whose slug a deploy refuses to read is left a subject.
A container recipe naming no repository is no subject of the container recipe kind.
A recipe naming a repository is the one a deploy pushes; one naming none is built where it runs.
A subject stating no cooldown carries the cooldown every service waits by default.
A subject naming services it deploys after carries their slugs alone.
The subjects of a kind come back ordered by slug.
Nothing here says whether a subject wants a deploy.
Nothing here reads what a deploy last put up.

definition: every thing of one kind a deploy could be run for, and what each states about being run
